transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doc, I guess what finally got me in here is that over these past few months, my mind just keeps jumping to every little thing. Like every single CB chirp catches my ear. And let me tell you, the chatter on the CB has been absolutely wild lately, especially down on I-40 with all that bridge construction. Guys are just complaining non-stop about the delays. 

But yeah, every chirp, or every fuel price sign I pass... which, by the way, have you seen what they're charging for diesel at the Flying J lately? It's highway robbery. I don't know how the independent guys are even keeping their rigs on the road with rates the way they are. 

But anyway, where was I? Right, I just keep getting all these new ideas while I'm driving, and my brain is just going, going, going, and I end up missing details I normally never miss. Like I completely blew past a client’s delivery note the other day. Or I'll forget who I promised to call back. Shoot, I think I still owe my brother a call from like three weeks ago about his truck's transmission...
Do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety when you're not driving?

Oh, yeah, definitely. If I sit still for too long, I get real antsy. It's like my motor's still running, so I just keep finding extra jobs for myself. Even when I'm off the clock, I'm sitting at the kitchen table rewriting my route plans, trying to shave off a few miles here and there. Or I'll be calling up the new drivers after hours just to check on 'em. 

We got this one kid, barely twenty-one, just got his CDL, and I swear he doesn't know how to properly secure a flatbed load to save his life. I had to talk him through throwing straps over the phone for like an hour the other night because he was terrified of the DOT scales down in Missouri. Those Missouri scales, they do not mess around, let me tell you. They will write you up for a muddy mudflap if they're in a bad mood. 

But anyway, yeah, and then at home I'm just fixing things non-stop. I took apart the whole lawnmower carburetor on Tuesday just because it was sputtering a little bit... which reminds me, I need to swing by AutoZone for a new spark plug before they close today. But sitting on the couch watching TV? No, I just can't do it right now.
Do you often act on these new ideas without thinking them through?

Well, I guess... I don't really know if I do them without thinking. I mean, they seem like good ideas at the time, you know? Like the other day, I got this idea to completely reorganize my toolboxes in the cab. I usually keep my wrenches on the left and the socket sets on the right, but I figured, what if I sort them by metric and standard instead? 

And speaking of metric, I had a heck of a time finding a 10mm socket when I was working on that lawnmower. I swear, 10mm sockets just vanish into thin air. You could buy a hundred of 'em and within a week, they're all gone. I think there's a black hole somewhere just sucking them up. My buddy Dave—he runs a route up to Chicago—he says he keeps a spare 10mm on a chain around his neck like a dog tag. Chicago's rough this time of year, though, the wind coming off the lake just cuts right through you. 

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, acting on ideas. I don't know, I just do things when they pop into my head. I don't really stop to think about whether it's a good time to do it or not.
Are these changes in your behavior and thinking causing problems for you at work or with your relationships?

Well, I mean... yeah, it's definitely causing some friction. Like at work, I've been having to ask dispatch to repeat things, and a couple of my clients too. I missed some details on some sales follow-ups because I'm just chasing ten different ideas at once. Which, speaking of dispatch, they hired this new guy, Greg, and I swear he mumbles into the radio on purpose. You can't hear a word he says over the engine noise. I told him he needs to eat the mic a little closer, but he just gets all defensive. Dispatchers, man, they sit in their air-conditioned offices and think they know everything about the road. They don't know what it's like when you're pulling 80,000 pounds up a six percent grade in the rain. 

And rain... man, it's been coming down buckets lately. I had to replace my wiper blades twice this season already. You buy those cheap ones at the truck stop and they just streak up your windshield after a week. I always tell the younger guys, invest in the good silicone ones, but they never listen. 

But yeah, at home... it's not great either. My wife and my daughter, they've been kind of walking on eggshells around me lately. I'm trying to help out, you know, fixing things and getting stuff done around the house, but I can tell I'm just stressing them out. I'm adding strain when I'm supposed to be helping. My daughter's got her senior prom coming up, and she's all stressed about the dress, and I tried to help her figure out a better way to organize her closet for it, and she just snapped at me. Kids these days, they just don't want to hear it.
Do you feel like these changes in your thinking and behavior are affecting your overall well-being?

Overall well-being? I mean... I'm not really sure what you mean by that. I haven't really stopped to take my own temperature, so to speak. I feel physically okay, mostly. Well, except my lower back, but that's just from the seats in these new Freightliners. The company says they're top-of-the-line ergonomic, but you sit in one bouncing down I-95 for eleven hours and tell me how ergonomic it feels. 

My buddy Earl, he actually bought one of those purple gel seat cushions you see on those late-night infomercials. He swears by it, says it's like sitting on a cloud. But Earl also eats those roller grill jalapeño hot dogs from the Flying J for breakfast every single morning, so I don't exactly trust his judgment on health and wellness, you know? Those hot dogs just sit there spinning under that heat lamp for God knows how long. I ate one back in '98 outside of Omaha and I swear my stomach didn't forgive me for a solid week. Omaha's got some incredible steakhouses, though, if you ever actually have the time to park the rig and go into town. There's this one place right off the interstate... 

Wait, what were we talking about? My well-being? Yeah, I don't know. I guess I haven't really noticed it taking a hit or anything.
Are you feeling overwhelmed by these changes in your thinking and behavior?

Overwhelmed? I don't... I wouldn't say overwhelmed, exactly. I mean, my mind is definitely going a mile a minute, but I'm keeping up with it. Mostly. It's kind of like when you're going downhill with a heavy load and you let the engine brake do the work, you know? You're moving fast, but you're still holding the steering wheel. 

Speaking of steering wheels, they changed the grip on the new models we just got in the fleet. It's this weird synthetic leather stuff that gets super slick if your hands sweat even a little bit. I tried putting one of those steering wheel covers on it—the ones you get at the truck stop with the eagles or the American flags on them—but it just slid right off when I was making a tight turn into a loading dock in Pittsburgh. Pittsburgh is a nightmare to drive in, by the way. The roads make no sense, it's all hills and bridges, and everyone drives like they're late for the Super Bowl. My cousin lived there for a few years, worked at a steel mill before it shut down. He used to make these incredible kielbasa sandwiches...

But, uh, no, I don't think I'm overwhelmed. Just... busy in the head, I guess.
Are you feeling like you're losing control because of all these thoughts and activities?

Losing control? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm the one behind the wheel, right? You don't drive a rig for twenty-five years if you don't know how to stay in control. You gotta be hyper-aware of everything around you. Like the other day, I was coming down through the Appalachians, and you really have to watch those four-wheelers. People in cars, they have no respect for the stopping distance of a semi. This guy in a little silver Honda Civic just zipped right in front of me and slammed on his brakes because he almost missed his exit. 

And those Civics, man, they run forever if you take care of them. My daughter wanted one for her first car, but I told her, no way, we're getting you something with a little more steel around you. We ended up finding this old Volvo station wagon. Built like a tank. Ugly as sin, kind of a faded mustard yellow color, but you could probably drive it through a brick wall and barely scratch the bumper. We had to replace the alternator on it about a month after we bought it, which was a real pain because European cars always need those special metric wrenches. I spent three hours tearing apart my garage looking for a 10-millimeter socket. Why is it always the 10-millimeter that goes missing? You could buy a pack of fifty of them and they'd all vanish into thin air by the end of the week. 

But, uh... what was the question? Losing control? Yeah, no, I'm definitely still in control. Just got a lot going on up here, that's all.
Are you feeling like these changes in your thinking and behavior are significantly interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Interfering? Well... I guess maybe a little bit, if I'm being honest. Like at work, I've been having to ask dispatch and some of my clients to repeat details that I normally would have locked down the first time. And I missed a couple of sales follow-ups recently because I was just... chasing too many ideas at once, you know? 

Speaking of dispatch, they hired this new guy, Greg. Nice enough kid, but he talks so fast you can barely understand him over the CB. He sounds like one of those auctioneers, you know? 'Going once, going twice, sold to the man in the back!' I went to a livestock auction once with my uncle down in Texas. Man, the smell of that place... you don't forget that. But they had these incredible brisket sandwiches at the concession stand. Texas barbecue is just a whole different ballgame. They use mesquite wood, mostly, which gives it this really sharp, smoky flavor. I tried smoking a brisket in my backyard last summer, but I couldn't get the temperature right on the smoker. It's a real art form, keeping that heat steady for twelve hours. 

But anyway, yeah, work's been a little messy. And at home... well, my wife and daughter, they've been kind of walking on eggshells around me lately. I can tell I'm adding strain to the house when I'm supposed to be the one keeping things steady. So, yeah, I guess it's bleeding over a bit.
Are you feeling distressed or upset by these changes in your thinking and behavior?

Distressed? I don't know if I'd use the word distressed. Maybe just... frustrated? Like, I know my brain is doing this thing, but I can't quite get it to settle down. It's like trying to idle a truck when the RPMs just want to keep revving. 

You know, speaking of revving, my neighbor two houses down bought one of those old muscle cars, a '69 Charger, I think. Beautiful car, cherry red, but he's out there in his driveway every Saturday morning at 7 AM tuning the carburetor. Vroom, vroom, vroom. Wakes up the whole neighborhood. I don't mind it so much because I'm usually up by 5 anyway, but my wife, she gets furious. She needs her sleep, especially since she started that new shift at the hospital. Working nights really messes with your circadian rhythm. I read an article in one of those waiting room magazines once about how night shift workers have a higher risk of all sorts of health problems. Something about the lack of sunlight messing with your vitamin D levels. I try to make sure I get plenty of sun when I'm on the road, keep the window down, get that trucker's tan on my left arm. 

But, uh, no, I'm not really upset about it. Just... it is what it is, you know? Just trying to manage it.
How long have you been experiencing this rapid thinking and constant stream of ideas?

How long? Let's see... I'd say it's been about seven months now. Yeah, right around the time my daughter moved back home. Things got a little chaotic, and I was just trying to keep everything steady, you know? Keep the plates spinning. 

It's funny how kids always end up coming back, isn't it? Like boomerang kids, they call them. She brought all her stuff, boxed up in these flimsy cardboard things she got from the grocery store. I told her, you gotta use the heavy-duty moving boxes from U-Haul if you don't want the bottoms falling out. I learned that the hard way when my wife and I moved into our first apartment. We were carrying a box of her grandmother's china up three flights of stairs, and boom—bottom gives out, plates everywhere. Sounded like a bomb went off in the stairwell. We spent hours picking up those tiny little pieces with a dustpan. 

And you know, dustpans nowadays, they don't make them like they used to. They're all cheap plastic that snaps if you step on it wrong. My dad had this old metal one, heavy gauge steel, probably weighed two pounds. You could use it as a shovel if you had to. He kept it in the garage right next to his workbench. He was always tinkering with something out there, fixing lawnmowers, sharpening mower blades... he had this grinder wheel that threw sparks everywhere. 

But yeah, anyway, it's been about seven months since she moved back and all this started up.
Are you having difficulty completing tasks at work or at home due to your racing thoughts and constant stream of ideas?

Well, yeah, like I was saying earlier... it's definitely making things harder. At work, I'm having to ask dispatch and my clients to repeat details that I really should have tracked the first time around. And I know a couple of my sales follow-ups slipped right through the cracks because I was just... chasing too many ideas at once, you know? 

Speaking of chasing ideas, I saw this documentary the other night about tornadoes. Storm chasers, they call them. These guys drive these heavily armored trucks right into the path of an F5 tornado just to drop some sensors in it. It's crazy! They reinforce the glass with polycarbonate or something so the hail doesn't smash through. Hail in the Midwest can get as big as softballs, you know. I drove through a hailstorm in Nebraska once in my rig, and it sounded like somebody was firing a machine gun at the roof of the cab. Dented the hood all up. Had to take it into the body shop in Omaha, and the guy there—real character, had a glass eye—he told me he sees fifty trucks a year with the exact same damage. 

But, uh, where was I? Oh, right, completing tasks. Yeah, so work's been tough, and at home... it's the same deal. My wife and daughter have been walking on eggshells around me. I can tell I'm adding strain to the house when I'm supposed to be the one helping keep things together. So yeah, it's definitely getting in the way.
Are you feeling like you're unable to fulfill your responsibilities at work or at home because of these changes in your thinking and behavior?

Well, yeah, like I just said, it's... it's definitely affecting things. I mean, I'm supposed to be the one providing, right? But out on the road, I'm having to ask dispatch to repeat the load details, or I'm missing things the clients tell me. And the sales side of things, I've completely dropped the ball on a couple of follow-ups because my brain is just zooming off in ten different directions. 

It's like when you're driving down the interstate and you see a billboard for a diner, and suddenly you're thinking about pancakes, and then maple syrup, and then you're wondering how they tap the trees in Vermont. I drove through Vermont once in the fall, absolutely gorgeous. The leaves turn these incredible shades of red and gold. They call them "leaf peepers," the tourists who drive up just to look at the trees. Clogs up the highways like you wouldn't believe. Try maneuvering an eighteen-wheeler through a two-lane mountain road when there's a line of minivans going twenty miles an hour under the speed limit just to take pictures out the window. It'll drive you crazy. You really have to rely on your engine brake going down those grades, otherwise you'll cook your brakes right off the truck. You smell that burning brake pad smell, and you know somebody's in trouble. 

But yeah, the responsibilities... I'm just not handling them right. And at home, it's the same thing. My wife and my daughter, they're just tiptoeing around me, walking on eggshells. I'm supposed to be helping keep the house together, especially with my daughter moving back, but I know I'm just adding more stress to the whole situation. So, yeah, I'm definitely not fulfilling my end of the bargain lately.
Are you finding it harder to do everyday tasks because of your racing thoughts?

Yeah, everyday tasks... it's just like I was saying, it's really getting tough. At work, I'm having to ask dispatch to repeat things, and clients too. I'm missing details I normally wouldn't. And those sales follow-ups, I missed a couple of them because my brain is just... it's like a television when someone's flipping the channels too fast. 

Speaking of televisions, did you know they don't make plasma screens anymore? It's all LED and OLED now. I had this great plasma TV back in the early 2000s. Cost me an arm and a leg, but the picture quality was unbelievable. The blacks were so deep, you know? Not like the grayish-black you get on cheap screens. I used to watch all the Sunday football games on it. My buddies would come over, we'd order pizzas from this place down the street... Mario's, I think it was called. Best garlic knots in the city. They'd tie the dough up in these little knots and just drench them in butter and garlic. You'd smell like garlic for three days afterwards, but it was worth it. Mario, the owner, he was this big guy with a mustache, always had flour on his apron. He moved back to Italy a few years ago, sold the place to some corporate chain. The pizza just isn't the same anymore. It tastes like cardboard now. 

But, uh, anyway... the tasks. Yeah. At home, it's just like I mentioned before. My wife and daughter are walking on eggshells around me. I'm supposed to be the one helping keep things stable, but I know I'm just adding strain to the house. Everything's just harder to get done.
Are you feeling like these changes in your thinking and behavior are causing you a lot of distress or discomfort?

Well, yeah, distress... I mean, it's definitely bothering me. Like I've been trying to explain, it's really messing with my daily life. At work, I'm constantly having to ask dispatch and my clients to repeat themselves because I just can't track the details like I usually do. And I've completely missed a couple of sales follow-ups just because my brain is running in a million different directions, chasing all these ideas. 

Speaking of chasing ideas, did you know that Thomas Edison had over a thousand patents? A thousand! The guy just never stopped inventing things. The lightbulb, the phonograph... he even invented this weird concrete house concept that totally flopped. Imagine living in a house made entirely of poured concrete, even the furniture. You'd stub your toe on a concrete bedframe in the middle of the night and break your foot. I broke my toe once, actually. Dropped a wrench on it while I was changing a tire on my rig just outside of Albuquerque. The sky out there in New Mexico is something else, man. They call it the Land of Enchantment, and they aren't kidding. The sunsets look like a painting, all purple and orange and pink. I stopped at this little roadside stand there and bought some green chile beef jerky. Hottest thing I've ever eaten in my life, I swear. I had to drink a whole gallon of water just to get the feeling back in my tongue. 

But yeah, the distress... it's just really frustrating. Especially at home. My wife and my daughter, they're just walking on eggshells around me all the time. I'm supposed to be the one helping keep things together, especially with my daughter being back home, but I know I'm just making everything more stressful for them. So yeah, it's definitely causing a lot of discomfort for me, and for everyone else.
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities at home or work due to these changes in your thinking and behavior?

Well, yeah, I mean, I feel like we just covered this, but... yeah, it's definitely a problem. Like I said, at work, I'm constantly having to get dispatch or the clients to repeat themselves. I just can't seem to hold onto the details. And those sales follow-ups, I've let a couple of them slip right through the cracks because my brain is just chasing a hundred different ideas at once. 

Speaking of chasing things, did you ever see that movie Twister? The one from the nineties with Bill Paxton and Helen Hunt? They were chasing tornadoes all over Oklahoma. I drove through a bad storm in Oklahoma once. The sky turned this weird, bruised green color, and the wind was blowing so hard I thought it was going to tip my rig right over. You really have to know how to handle a truck in high winds. You can't just grip the wheel and pray; you have to steer into the wind a little bit, keep your momentum steady. I saw a guy in a box truck get blown clean off the shoulder into a ditch. Took them three tow trucks to haul him out. Tow truck drivers, man, those guys are fearless. They'll be out there on the side of the highway with cars flying past them at eighty miles an hour, just hooking up a winch like it's nothing. I always try to move over a lane when I see flashing lights on the shoulder. It's the law, you know, but a lot of people just don't care. They're too busy looking at their phones or messing with the radio. 

But anyway, yeah, the responsibilities. It's tough. And at home, it's exactly what I was saying before. My wife and my daughter, they're just tiptoeing around, walking on eggshells. I'm supposed to be the one helping keep the peace and keeping things running, but I can tell I'm just adding more strain to the whole house. So, yeah, I'm definitely having trouble meeting my responsibilities.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or failing to finish tasks because you get distracted?

Yeah, distracted... that's exactly what finally got me in here. Over these past few months, my mind just keeps jumping to every little thing. Like, every single CB chirp, or a fuel price sign on the side of the highway, or just some random new idea that pops into my head. And because of that, I'm missing details I normally never miss. Like a client's delivery note, or who I promised to call back. 

Speaking of CB radios, did you know they used to be huge in the seventies? Like, everyone had one, not just truckers. They even had all those movies about it, like Smokey and the Bandit. Burt Reynolds, man, what a legend. He had that black Trans Am with the gold bird on the hood. I wanted one of those cars so bad when I was a kid. My uncle had a Camaro, which was pretty close, but it wasn't a Trans Am. He used to take me for rides in it on the weekends. We'd go down to this old drive-in theater that used to be on the edge of town. They'd show double features for like, three bucks. We saw Jaws there once. Scared the living daylights out of me. I didn't go swimming in a lake for two years after that, even though I knew sharks don't live in lakes. Well, except for bull sharks, I guess. I saw a documentary once that said bull sharks can swim up rivers. Imagine fishing in a river and catching a shark! 

But yeah, anyway... the mistakes. It's just like I said, I'm getting distracted by every little thing out on the road, and I end up forgetting to call people back or missing those delivery notes. It's really frustrating.
Do you often have difficulty sustaining focus during tasks or activities that require prolonged mental effort?

Well, yeah, doc, I feel like I'm a broken record here, but it's exactly what I was just saying a second ago. Prolonged effort? Forget about it. If I have to focus on something for a long stretch, it's just not happening. Like I said, my mind just jumps to the next new idea, or I get completely derailed by a fuel price sign out the window. 

Speaking of fuel prices, they are just out of control lately, aren't they? I remember when diesel was under two bucks a gallon. Now you pull up to a pump out in California and you're basically taking out a second mortgage just to fill the tanks. California is beautiful, though. Have you ever driven the Pacific Coast Highway? Unbelievable views. I took my wife out there for our tenth anniversary. We rented this little convertible, a Mustang. Cherry red. It drove like an absolute dream. Ford really knew what they were doing when they brought back that retro look for the newer Mustangs. My neighbor actually has a classic '69 Mach 1 sitting in his garage. He never even drives it, just pulls it out to the driveway and polishes it on Sundays. Seems like a total waste of a good machine, if you ask me. Cars are meant to be driven. You can't just keep a thoroughbred locked in the stable, you know? 

But anyway, what were we... right, focusing. Yeah, it's just like I told you, that's the whole reason I'm sitting here in this office. I can't sustain my attention on the paperwork or the long hauls right now, and I end up missing those delivery notes or forgetting who I promised to call back. Every single time the CB chirps, my brain just completely abandons whatever I was trying to concentrate on.
Are you feeling like these changes in your thinking and behavior are making it hard for you to get along with others or do your job?

Doc, I gotta ask, are you testing my memory today? Because I swear we literally just went over this a few minutes ago. But yeah, it is definitely making it hard. Like I was saying before, at work, I'm having to ask dispatch and the clients to repeat all these details that I really should have tracked the first time. And a couple of my sales follow-ups have completely slipped through the cracks because I'm just chasing way too many ideas at once. 

Speaking of chasing ideas, did I ever tell you about the time I thought I was going to invent a new kind of windshield wiper for the big rigs? I had this whole blueprint drawn out on a diner napkin somewhere in Nebraska. The idea was to have a heated blade that would melt the ice before it could even stick to the glass. Ice on the windshield is a nightmare when you're hauling eighty thousand pounds through a blizzard. I was stuck in a whiteout in Wyoming once, on I-80. The snow was coming down so thick you couldn't see the hood of your own truck. They ended up shutting down the interstate and we were all just parked on the shoulder for fourteen hours. I had a load of frozen chicken in the back, so at least the cargo wasn't going to spoil, but man, sitting in a cab for that long gets old fast. You end up listening to the same three country stations on the radio until you know all the words to every song. I actually kind of like classic country, though. Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson, the real outlaws. Music today just sounds like it was made by a computer. 

But anyway, getting along with others... yeah, it's exactly what I mentioned earlier. It's really rough at home right now. My wife and my daughter have just been walking on eggshells around me. I'm supposed to be the one helping out and keeping things solid, but I can tell I'm just adding a ton of strain to the house instead. So, yeah, I'd say it's definitely making my job and my family life pretty difficult.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

Interrupting people? No, I don't really think I do that. I mean, maybe I get a little excited sometimes, but I don't just blurt things out before they're done talking. I usually let people finish. 

Though, you know, it's funny you mention talking, because my wife says I've been talking a lot louder lately. Not interrupting, just loud. Like I'm trying to talk over the engine noise even when I'm sitting in the living room. It's a habit you pick up when you drive a Peterbilt for twenty years. Those engines roar, especially the older ones. Nothing beats the sound of a big diesel engine, though. It's like a heartbeat. When I was a kid, my dad used to take me to truck pulls at the county fair. You ever been to one of those? They hook these massive tractors up to a weighted sled and see how far they can drag it through the mud. The noise is deafening, and the smoke just pours out of the stacks. We used to get funnel cake afterward. I haven't had a good funnel cake in years. The ones they sell at the amusement parks now are always too greasy and they skimp on the powdered sugar. You gotta have a mountain of powdered sugar on a funnel cake, that's the whole point. And maybe some strawberries, if you're feeling fancy. My daughter loves strawberries. We used to go strawberry picking every June at this farm out past the county line, before she got to be a teenager and decided hanging out with her old man was uncool. 

But no, to answer your question... I don't really have a problem with blurting things out or cutting people off. I might get a bit loud, but I let folks say their piece.
Are you feeling like these changes in your thinking and behavior are significantly affecting your ability to function at work or get along with your family?

Doc, seriously? Are you messing with me right now? I feel like we're just going in circles here. I literally just told you this, like, two minutes ago. But yeah, it's definitely messing things up. Like I just said, at work, I'm having dispatch and the clients repeat all these details I should have caught the first time. And some of my sales follow-ups completely slipped through the cracks because I'm chasing a hundred ideas at once. 

It's funny how things slip through the cracks, though. Reminds me of this one time I lost my favorite pair of aviators. I swear they just vanished into thin air. I looked everywhere—under the seats of the rig, in the sleeper berth, even checked the fridge at home just in case I lost my mind. Turns out, they had fallen behind the center console of my wife's car. I only found them three months later when I was trying to fish out a dropped french fry. Those fries from that drive-thru on Route 9 are the best, though. Always perfectly salted. You know how some places just hand you a soggy, unsalted potato? It's a crime against food. If I'm paying for fries, I want that crunch. I actually bought a deep fryer for the house a few years back thinking I could make them just as good, but the oil smell just lingers in the kitchen for days. My wife hated it. She made me put it out in the garage, and now it's just sitting there collecting dust next to my old bowling ball. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. Had a 180 average, which isn't pro level or anything, but it kept me out of trouble.

But yeah, anyway, the family stuff. Like I said before, it's rough. My wife and daughter are just walking on eggshells around me. I'm supposed to be the guy keeping things steady and helping out, but I know I'm just adding a ton of strain to the house right now. So, yes, it's definitely affecting my job and my family.

But anyway, what were we... right, focusing. Yeah, it's just like I told you, that's the whole reason I'm sitting here in this office. I can't sustain my attention on the paperwork or the long hauls right now, and I end up missing those delivery notes or forgetting who I promised to call back. Every single time the CB chirps, my brain just completely abandons whatever I was trying to concentrate on.

patient.answer:
Doc, I gotta ask, are you testing my memory today? Because I swear we literally just went over this a few minutes ago. But yeah, it is definitely making it hard. Like I was saying before, at work, I'm having to ask dispatch and the clients to repeat all these details that I really should have tracked the first time. And a couple of my sales follow-ups have completely slipped through the cracks because I'm just chasing way too many ideas at once. 

Speaking of chasing ideas, did I ever tell you about the time I thought I was going to invent a new kind of windshield wiper for the big rigs? I had this whole blueprint drawn out on a diner napkin somewhere in Nebraska. The idea was to have a heated blade that would melt the ice before it could even stick to the glass. Ice on the windshield is a nightmare when you're hauling eighty thousand pounds through a blizzard. I was stuck in a whiteout in Wyoming once, on I-80. The snow was coming down so thick you couldn't see the hood of your own truck. They ended up shutting down the interstate and we were all just parked on the shoulder for fourteen hours. I had a load of frozen chicken in the back, so at least the cargo wasn't going to spoil, but man, sitting in a cab for that long gets old fast. You end up listening to the same three country stations on the radio until you know all the words to every song. I actually kind of like classic country, though. Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson, the real outlaws. Music today just sounds like it was made by a computer. 

But anyway, getting along with others... yeah, it's exactly what I mentioned earlier. It's really rough at home right now. My wife and my daughter have just been walking on eggshells around me. I'm supposed to be the one helping out and keeping things solid, but I can tell I'm just adding a ton of strain to the house instead. So, yeah, I'd say it's definitely making my job and my family life pretty difficult.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), specifically the presence of impulsivity
doctor.question: Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about impulsivity (interrupting others or blurting out answers), which is not covered by the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Interrupting people? No, I don't really think I do that. I mean, maybe I get a little excited sometimes, but I don't just blurt things out before they're done talking. I usually let people finish. 

Though, you know, it's funny you mention talking, because my wife says I've been talking a lot louder lately. Not interrupting, just loud. Like I'm trying to talk over the engine noise even when I'm sitting in the living room. It's a habit you pick up when you drive a Peterbilt for twenty years. Those engines roar, especially the older ones. Nothing beats the sound of a big diesel engine, though. It's like a heartbeat. When I was a kid, my dad used to take me to truck pulls at the county fair. You ever been to one of those? They hook these massive tractors up to a weighted sled and see how far they can drag it through the mud. The noise is deafening, and the smoke just pours out of the stacks. We used to get funnel cake afterward. I haven't had a good funnel cake in years. The ones they sell at the amusement parks now are always too greasy and they skimp on the powdered sugar. You gotta have a mountain of powdered sugar on a funnel cake, that's the whole point. And maybe some strawberries, if you're feeling fancy. My daughter loves strawberries. We used to go strawberry picking every June at this farm out past the county line, before she got to be a teenager and decided hanging out with her old man was uncool. 

But no, to answer your question... I don't really have a problem with blurting things out or cutting people off. I might get a bit loud, but I let folks say their piece.

patient.answer:
Doc, seriously? Are you messing with me right now? I feel like we're just going in circles here. I literally just told you this, like, two minutes ago. But yeah, it's definitely messing things up. Like I just said, at work, I'm having dispatch and the clients repeat all these details I should have caught the first time. And some of my sales follow-ups completely slipped through the cracks because I'm chasing a hundred ideas at once. 

It's funny how things slip through the cracks, though. Reminds me of this one time I lost my favorite pair of aviators. I swear they just vanished into thin air. I looked everywhere—under the seats of the rig, in the sleeper berth, even checked the fridge at home just in case I lost my mind. Turns out, they had fallen behind the center console of my wife's car. I only found them three months later when I was trying to fish out a dropped french fry. Those fries from that drive-thru on Route 9 are the best, though. Always perfectly salted. You know how some places just hand you a soggy, unsalted potato? It's a crime against food. If I'm paying for fries, I want that crunch. I actually bought a deep fryer for the house a few years back thinking I could make them just as good, but the oil smell just lingers in the kitchen for days. My wife hated it. She made me put it out in the garage, and now it's just sitting there collecting dust next to my old bowling ball. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. Had a 180 average, which isn't pro level or anything, but it kept me out of trouble.

But yeah, anyway, the family stuff. Like I said before, it's rough. My wife and daughter are just walking on eggshells around me. I'm supposed to be the guy keeping things steady and helping out, but I know I'm just adding a ton of strain to the house right now. So, yes, it's definitely affecting my job and my family.
